narrative.overview:
A premium, editorial training space that has the warmth of a private studio and the precision of a well-designed strength program. Ivory paper, ink black, muted gold, elegant serif headlines, atmospheric gym photography, and refined layouts. It should feel sophisticated and athletic, never clinical and never over-decorated. The public site reads as one long document, not a stack of modules. Every section opens the same way, sits on the same grid and shares one spacing ramp, so no section looks like it was added later.

The system has three registers that share one palette family. The **public site** (the Atelier proper) is about three-quarters light: warm paper where the reading happens, with the black ground saved for the moments that earn drama (the opening, the bundle, the closing ask, the footer). The **coaching portal** (`/my-coaching`) stays on the same warm light ground, but it serves clarity, usability and effortless one-handed mobile use over decoration. The **course world** (Training Foundations, Masterclass and the admin area) is a separate dark, luxury register: charcoal, cream and gold, with Cormorant Garamond and Montserrat.

Density is generous on the public site (long line-heights, wide section padding, light 300-weight body text) and tighter in the portal and admin, where the job is getting a task done.
keyCharacteristics: One accent family (gold) on ivory and black. No other brand hues.
Square corners, hairline rules and underline inputs on the public site. No boxes and no shadows.
Serif display type, light sans body text, and small wide-tracked uppercase labels.
Slow, eased motion (`cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)`): ink-fill buttons, drawn rules, line-by-line reveals. Every animation respects reduced motion.
Tone changes between dark and light sections blend across an eased gradient band, never on a hard edge.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Gold is the only brand hue. New colors or fonts need Lisa's explicit approval. Tints of the existing tokens at reduced opacity are how the system gets its range.

rules.name: The Status-Only Rule
rules.body: Green, terracotta and red exist only to report state (success, warning, error). They are never decoration, never brand, and never appear on the public marketing pages.

rules.name: The Two Golds Rule
rules.body: Use Antique Gold on light grounds and Champagne Gold on dark grounds. Swapping them breaks contrast in one direction or the other.

rules.name: The Readable Contrast Rule
rules.body: On the coaching platform and in all new work, text meets WCAG 2.2 AA: 4.5:1 for text under 24px (under 18.66px if bold), and 3:1 for larger text and for UI marks such as borders, icons and focus rings. Measured on light grounds: Warm Taupe passes for text of any size (5.4:1 on ivory, 5.7:1 on white). Antique Gold (3.1:1 on ivory), Success Green (3.2:1 on white) and Warning Terracotta (3.2:1 on white) pass only as large text or as marks. Champagne Gold on ivory (2.1:1) fails as both text and marks. Small text therefore uses Ink Text or Warm Taupe, and color is never the only signal of state: always pair it with a word or an icon.

rules.name: The Same Opening Rule
rules.body: Every public section opens with eyebrow, then a short drawn gold rule (54px), then the headline. Repeating one opening is most of what makes the site read as one document.

rules.name: The Light Body Rule
rules.body: Body copy is weight 300. Emphasis comes from the serif and from gold italics, never from bold body text.

rules.name: The Readable Floor Rule
rules.body: On the coaching platform and in new work, secondary labels (eyebrows, field labels, figure labels, metadata) are at least 12px, and body text is 16px, the preferred size everywhere and especially on mobile. Some existing portal and admin screens fall below this. They will be brought up as part of the coaching platform UI/UX work, not changed piecemeal.

rules.name: The Seamless Ground Rule
rules.body: Never change tone (light to dark) on a hard edge. Use `ToneShift`, a smoothstep-eased gradient band (`clamp(42px, 9vw, 150px)`, 20px on phones) whose halves carry `data-tone` so the nav flips at the midpoint.

rules.name: The Three-Quarters Light Rule
rules.body: Most of a public page is paper. Dark grounds are reserved for the opening, the bundle, the closing ask and the footer.

rules.name: The No-Box Rule
rules.body: On the public site, separate content with hairline rules and space, never with drop shadows or bordered cards.

rules.name: The Square Atelier Rule
rules.body: Square corners on every public page. Rounded corners belong to the portal, course and admin apps only.

rules.name: The Thumb Target Rule
rules.body: Every tap target on the coaching platform is at least 44×44px, well above the WCAG 2.2 AA minimum of 24px, with at least 8px between neighbouring targets. Clients log sets one-handed mid-workout, so primary actions sit within thumb reach. Every interactive element shows a visible focus ring that meets 3:1 contrast.

dos: **Do** build public sections from the shared furniture in `src/components/preview/d/Sections.tsx` (`SectionD`, `OpenD`, `MarkerListD`, `ModuleRailD`, `PriceBlockD`, `QaListD`) so new pages inherit the rhythm.
**Do** use only the `--d-*` spacing ramp, `--d-gutter` and `--d-max` for spacing and width on public pages.
**Do** put `ToneShift` between every light and dark ground, and set `data-tone` on every section so the nav can read it.
**Do** use Antique Gold for accents on light grounds and Champagne Gold on dark grounds.
**Do** honor `prefers-reduced-motion` in every reveal, rule and transition. The existing `Reveal`, `RevealLines` and `DrawRule` already do.

**Do** make coaching platform screens easy to read and use on a phone mid-workout: secondary labels at 12px or larger, body text at 16px, AA contrast, and tap targets of at least 44×44px (see the Readable Floor, Readable Contrast and Thumb Target rules).
**Do** use status colors only to report state.
donts: **Don't** introduce new colors or fonts without Lisa's explicit approval.
**Don't** round corners, add drop shadows or wrap content in bordered cards on public pages.
**Don't** change tone on a hard edge between sections.
**Don't** use bold body text. Use the serif or gold italics for emphasis.
**Don't** use green, terracotta or red on the public marketing pages, or anywhere as decoration.
**Don't** mix the course world's Cormorant and Montserrat into the public site, or the public site's Playfair and DM Sans into course modules.
**Don't** use fast, bouncy or springy easing. Motion here is slow and settles.
